answer: No: the aggregate consultation statistics (1,340 respondents, 58%/24%/18% split) and the anonymous free-text sentiment ('ruins the feel of the place') should not be folded into the CRM-modelled heritage documentation. The Scope of the CIDOC CRM narrative summarises the model's target as 'the curated, factual knowledge about the past at a human scale,' and explicitly names the analogous case: 'information relating to personnel, accounting, and visitor statistics, falls outside the Intended Scope of the CIDOC CRM.' A public-consultation poll is the same kind of administrative/management-process data as visitor statistics -- a numeric summary over an anonymous population, gathered to inform a present-day decision, not curated evidence about the landscape's design history. The free-text comments fare no better: CRM's documentary classes (E31 Document, E33 Linguistic Object, E89 Propositional Object) presuppose an identifiable object making propositions, traceable to an actor (P14/P94/authorship); several hundred anonymous comments folded into one aggregate sentiment have neither an identified author nor a determinate proposition, so they cannot be attached the way a named commentator's or curator's note could be. What CAN legitimately be recorded, if the trust wants provenance for the decision itself, is that a consultation activity took place -- E7 Activity, with P4 has time-span and P7 took place at -- as a fact about the management process, but that only records the event's occurrence, not the poll numbers or the sentiment content, which is what this question actually asked about.

rejected_alternatives.option: E7 Activity (for the poll content itself)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E7 can record that a consultation event occurred (time-span, place), but has no property that takes an aggregate statistic or a population's anonymous sentiment as its content -- only that the event happened, which is not what the question asks about recording.

Both require an identifiable item being assessed and, functionally, an assessor; a 58%-opposed figure over 1,340 anonymous respondents has no single identified subject and no identified assessor, so it does not fit the assignment/measurement pattern.

rejected_alternatives.option: E31 Document / E33 Linguistic Object / E89 Propositional Object
rejected_alternatives.why_not: These model identifiable items making propositions, traceable to authorship. Aggregated, anonymous free-text comments folded into 'public sentiment' are neither one identifiable document nor attributable to an actor, so the pattern used elsewhere for citing an identified source's opinion does not transfer.
